2026-08-18.whatHappened: This file held exactly 162 fingerprints, written by a single commit on 2026-07-21 and untouched for four weeks. 121 of them were never real. The sweep runs over the Storybook build, and that build was measuring something the product does not look like, for two independent reasons — both in the harness, neither in the components:
2026-08-18.harnessDefect1: `src/styles/storybook.css` `@source`d only `packages/ui`, while `.storybook/main.ts` has loaded `packages/widgets` and `packages/charts` stories since 04-T17. Tailwind v4 generates utilities from source TEXT, so every widget and chart story rendered with its class attributes intact and NO rules behind them. The widget families were 60% of the baseline.
2026-08-18.harnessDefect2: Nothing painted `--bg`/`--fg` on the preview body, so Storybook's own white body showed through. Under `data-theme="dark"` every story drew dark-theme FOREGROUNDS on a WHITE page, and axe resolves `color-contrast` against the nearest opaque ancestor — so the translucent tone tints composited over white and reported pairs the product never renders (dark `--pos` #3ecf8e on #e4f8ef at 1.8:1, against a token gate that passes the real pair at 4.5:1+). 123 of the 162 were dark-theme entries.
2026-08-18.thenWhat:
Fixing both exposed 27 violations the unstyled build had HIDDEN, and left 128 real ones. Those were then fixed rather than baselined: alpha-dimmed small text on the accent bubble and event chips (`text-accent-fg/70`, `opacity-80`) went to full opacity; six scrollable regions with no focusable content got `tabIndex` + a labelled role; `role="row"` containers whose children carried no cell role got `rowheader`/`cell`/`columnheader`; a `

2026-08-18.stillOpen: One entry, and it is a token decision rather than a component bug — see `acceptedWithRationale` below.

widgets-tables-datagrid--selection-and-b.what: A `danger` status Tag (`bg-danger-soft text-danger`) inside a SELECTED DataGrid row (`bg-accent-soft`) in dark theme. Measured 4.41:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement.
widgets-tables-datagrid--selection-and-b.whyNotFixedHere: It is not this component. Both tints are translucent by design, so a tone chip on a selected row composites tone-soft over accent-soft over the surface, and loses about a point of contrast doing it. Measuring that composition across the whole dark palette — 8 accents x 4 surfaces x 4 tones — finds 44 failing pairs, from 4.50 down to 3.54 (`black` accent, `--surface-3`, `danger`). This story is simply the one that renders it.
widgets-tables-datagrid--selection-and-b.whatTheGateDoesNotSee: `packages/tokens/scripts/contrast-check.mjs` measures `<tone>` on `<tone>-soft` over each SURFACE, and every one of those passes. It does not measure a soft tint over ANOTHER soft tint, which is what a selected row is. That gap is why 44 failing pairs read as zero.
widgets-tables-datagrid--selection-and-b.theDecisionItNeeds: One of three, and all three are palette-wide: (a) lower the dark soft-tint alpha — 14% -> 12% clears the DataGrid case at 4.60 and is a visible change to every tinted chip in dark; (b) make tone-soft opaque (mix with the surface instead of transparent), which removes the stacking entirely and costs the tint its adaptability; (c) stop washing selected rows behind chip-bearing cells. Whichever is chosen, the gate should gain the composition so it stops being invisible. Not decided unilaterally inside an accessibility sweep.
